edges.description: Truncated plakoglobin destabilizes the cardiomyocyte desmosome at the intercalated disc, impairing mechanical cell-cell adhesion.
The same plakoglobin defect weakens desmosomal adhesion in epidermal keratinocytes and the hair follicle, producing palmoplantar keratoderma and woolly hair.
Failure of mutant plakoglobin to localize at the intercalated disc remodels connexin43 gap junctions, creating an early arrhythmogenic substrate that precedes overt structural disease.
Desmosomal disruption can redistribute plakoglobin to the nucleus, where it suppresses canonical Wnt/beta-catenin signaling and switches on adipogenic and fibrogenic gene programs.
intermediate_mechanisms: Release and nuclear redistribution of plakoglobin after desmosomal disruption

edges.description: Progressive cardiomyocyte death is followed by fibrous and fatty replacement of the myocardium.
intermediate_mechanisms: Cardiomyocyte injury and apoptosis under repetitive wall stress

edges.description: Gap-junction remodeling slows myocardial conduction, contributing to the reentrant arrhythmogenic substrate.
intermediate_mechanisms: Reduced connexin43-mediated electrical coupling and slowed conduction

edges.description: Wnt suppression-driven adipogenic and fibrogenic gene programs promote fibrofatty replacement of myocardium.
intermediate_mechanisms: Adipogenic and fibrogenic transcriptional reprogramming of cardiac cells
edges.source: Nuclear plakoglobin and canonical Wnt suppression

edges.description: The fibrofatty substrate promotes malignant ventricular arrhythmias that can cause syncope and sudden cardiac death.
intermediate_mechanisms: Scar-related slow-conduction and reentrant arrhythmogenic substrate

nodes.description: Weakened desmosomal adhesion in epidermal keratinocytes and the hair follicle produces the ectodermal phenotype: diffuse non-epidermolytic palmoplantar keratoderma and woolly hair present from infancy.

evidence.reference_title: Naxos disease and Carvajal syndrome: cardiocutaneous disorders that highlight the pathogenesis and broaden the spectrum of arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy.
evidence.snippet: All patients had the hair and skin phenotype from infancy and developed ARVC by adolescence.

nodes.description: Loss of cardiomyocytes with fibrofatty or fibrous replacement, at subepicardial and mediomural layers and predominantly of the right ventricle, creates an arrhythmogenic substrate and progressive ventricular dysfunction. Left ventricular involvement occurs in a minority.

evidence.reference_title: Naxos disease and Carvajal syndrome: cardiocutaneous disorders that highlight the pathogenesis and broaden the spectrum of arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy.
evidence.snippet: characterized histologically by myocardial loss with fibrofatty or fibrous replacement at subepicardial and mediomural layers.

histopathology_terms.name: Fibrofatty myocardial replacement at subepicardial and mediomural layers

nodes.description: Mutant plakoglobin that fails to localize at the intercalated disc causes a significant reduction of connexin43 gap-junction protein in both ventricles, with smaller and fewer gap junctions. Desmosomal dysfunction also secondarily reduces the cardiac sodium channel NaV1.5 (SCN5A) at the intercalated disc. Together this gap-junction and sodium-channel remodeling forms an arrhythmogenic substrate that is present even before overt structural cardiomyopathy.

evidence.reference_title: Remodeling of myocyte gap junctions in arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy due to a deletion in plakoglobin (Naxos disease).
evidence.snippet: Connexin43 expression at intercellular junctions was reduced significantly in both right and left ventricles in all patients with Naxos disease.

evidence.reference_title: Remodeling of the cardiac sodium channel, connexin43, and plakoglobin at the intercalated disk in patients with arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy.
evidence.snippet: Immunoreactive signal levels of PKG, Cx43, and NaV1.5 were disturbed in 74%, 70%, and 65% of the patients, respectively.

evidence.reference_title: Remodeling of myocyte gap junctions in arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy due to a deletion in plakoglobin (Naxos disease).
evidence.snippet: Electron microscopy revealed smaller and fewer gap junctions interconnecting ventricular myocytes.

nodes.description: Plakoglobin deficiency destabilizes the cardiomyocyte desmosome at the intercalated disc, causing mechanical cell-cell adhesion failure. Under repetitive mechanical wall stress this leads to cardiomyocyte injury and death.

evidence.reference_title: Identification of a deletion in plakoglobin in arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy with palmoplantar keratoderma and woolly hair (Naxos disease).
evidence.snippet: the proteins involved in cell-cell adhesion play an important part in maintaining myocyte integrity, and when junctions are disrupted, cell death, and fibrofatty replacement occur.

evidence.reference_title: Naxos disease: cardiocutaneous syndrome due to cell adhesion defect.
evidence.snippet: Defects in the linking sites of these proteins can interrupt the contiguous chain of cell adhesion, particularly under conditions of increased mechanical stress or stretch, leading to cell death, progressive loss of myocardium and fibro-fatty replacement.

evidence.reference_title: Identification of a deletion in plakoglobin in arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy with palmoplantar keratoderma and woolly hair (Naxos disease).
evidence.snippet: A homozygous 2 base pair deletion in the plakoglobin gene was identified only in the 19 affected individuals. This deletion caused a frameshift and premature termination of the protein, which was shown by western blot analysis.

evidence.reference_title: Identification of a deletion in plakoglobin in arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy with palmoplantar keratoderma and woolly hair (Naxos disease).
evidence.snippet: 29 clinically unaffected family members were heterozygous for the mutation; 20 unrelated individuals from Naxos and 43 autosomal dominant ARVC probands were homozygous for the normal allele.

evidence.reference_title: A novel dominant mutation in plakoglobin causes arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy.
evidence.snippet: we report, for the first time, a dominant mutation in the gene encoding plakoglobin in a German family with ARVC but no cutaneous abnormalities. The mutation (S39_K40insS) is predicted to insert an extra serine residue at position 39 in the N-terminus of plakoglobin.

evidence.reference_title: Naxos disease in an Arab family is not caused by the Pk2157del2 mutation. Evidence for exclusion of the plakoglobin gene.
evidence.snippet: Absence of the Pk2157del2 frameshift in the affected child proved that Naxos disease in this Saudi Arab family is not caused by the same mutation

nodes.description: Desmosomal disruption can redistribute plakoglobin to the nucleus, where it reduces canonical Wnt/beta-catenin signaling through Tcf/Lef1, activating adipogenic and fibrogenic gene programs that drive the characteristic fibrofatty replacement. Confidence is PROVISIONAL for Naxos disease: the supporting evidence derives from desmoplakin (DSP) knockdown/knockout models rather than plakoglobin (JUP) loss, so its translational validity to the human JUP phenotype remains an open question (see the attached HUMAN_MODEL_MISMATCH discussion).

evidence.reference_title: Suppression of canonical Wnt/beta-catenin signaling by nuclear plakoglobin recapitulates phenotype of arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy.
evidence.snippet: The ensuing phenotype is increased expression of adipogenic and fibrogenic genes and accumulation of fat droplets.

nodes.description: Homozygous truncating variants in JUP (plakoglobin/gamma-catenin) produce a C-terminally truncated protein. Plakoglobin is a core armadillo-family protein of the desmosome and adherens junction, so its loss impairs junctional protein assembly at cell-cell contacts in tissues that depend on strong mechanical adhesion, including myocardium, epidermis, and hair follicle.

evidence.reference_title: Identification of a deletion in plakoglobin in arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy with palmoplantar keratoderma and woolly hair (Naxos disease).
evidence.snippet: This protein is a key component of desmosomes and adherens junctions, and is important for the tight adhesion of many cell types, including those in the heart and skin.

nodes.description: The arrhythmogenic substrate produces frequent ventricular ectopy and ventricular tachycardia (often of left bundle branch block morphology), causing syncope and a substantial risk of sudden cardiac death, with progressive structural disease and heart failure over time.

evidence.reference_title: Genotype-phenotype assessment in autosomal recessive arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy (Naxos disease) caused by a deletion in plakoglobin.
evidence.snippet: Of the 26 subjects who were affected homozygotes, 92% showed ECG abnormalities, 92% ventricular arrhythmias, 100% right ventricular structural alterations and 27% left ventricular involvement.
